source_title: U.S. bans imports from Chinese genomics companies over forced labour concerns
source_excerpt: Washington, United States The United States banned imports from three Chinese genomics companies on Wednesday (October 28, 2026) over claims they collected genetic material used to track persecuted ethnic minorities in China's Xinjiang region. The U.S. Department of Homeland Security (DHS) said BGI Genomics, MGI Tech and Shenzhen BGI Technology, also known as BGI Group, had been added to the Uyghur Forced Labor Prevention Act Entity List. China opposes U.S. ‘forced labour’ tariffs, calls for them to cancelled China opposes U.S. ‘forced labour’ tariffs, calls for them to cancelled This time, it (Washington) has again initiated ‌a Section 301 investigation and imposed unilateral tariffs on ​the grounds of 'forced labour,' and China firmly opposes ⁠it, said a statement by China’s Commerce Ministry China opposes U.S. ‘forced labour’ tariffs, calls for them to cancelled storyline 1 The list identifies entities working with Xinjiang's government "to recruit, transport, transfer, harbour or receive forced labour or Uyghurs, Kazakhs, Kyrgyz, or members of other persecuted groups out of Xinjiang." The United Nations warned in 2022 of possible crimes against humanity in the region, including the detention of more than a million Uyghurs and other Muslim minorities in camps. China has repeatedly and vehemently denied accusations of human rights abuses against the Uyghurs. According to the U.S. DHS, the companies "helped collect genetic material used to track persecuted ethnic minorities, including people subjected to forced labour, meaning work they could not freely refuse." Beijing said on Thursday (October 29, 2026) that it "strongly condemns" Washington's ban, which has "no factual basis". "The U.S. side continues to exploit the 'human rights' issue, using it as a pretext to pursue unilateral protectionism and bullying," a Chinese Ministry of Commerce spokesperson said in a statement.
